analyst_view.overall: Second-bottom Elche (11 points, one win in five, a late 1-1 at home to Levante on Monday) host third-placed Atlético (31 points, 3-0 winners at Getafe last Sunday) on Saturday evening; the numbers give Atlético a slight edge and about 2.5 goals. Atlético played Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday, and the previews expect Koke and Johnny Cardoso to start on the bench, with Pubill back from an ankle sprain; Lookman (knee, about a month) and Cuti Romero are out and counted, and one report says Sørloth has another muscle problem. Martín Anselmi's Elche have no suspensions but miss Lemar (counted), Rubén Sánchez and Houary, with Yago Santiago and Boayar doubts; playmaker Marc Aguado's return is unclear, as the previews disagree. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, already trimmed because both sides have scored less than usual lately and for Lemar, Lookman and Romero being out. Atlético's midfield rotation after Wednesday should not blunt Julián Álvarez, and Elche are still short of attackers, with Aguado's return unclear; these roughly balance, so I stay at 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, already lower for Atlético's low recent corner count. Simeone's side tend to let the home team push once ahead, which can give Elche corners, and Grimaldo's crossing gives Atlético some of their own, but nothing in this week's news changes the picture. I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already reflecting Atlético's quieter recent booking record and the past meetings. A home side near the bottom against a top-three team brings intensity, which the numbers see in Elche's recent cards, and no referee has been named yet, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots, already lifting Elche (+9.7%) because Atlético have allowed many shots lately. Resting Koke and Cardoso could leave a little more space, but Elche are short of forwards, so the two cancel and I stay at about 26.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already lowering Elche (-7.2%) for their poor recent accuracy. Whether Aguado plays is unclear and Atlético's attack still runs through Julián Álvarez, so I see no reason to move it and stay at about 8.3.
